A later2024 accompanied recording with a similar title is a distinct release and is not used as this2017 single's roster. tradition.name: Rogaland Musikk
tradition.lineage: Malmin with Åshild Vetrhus — Med Åshild Vetrhus (2025). Present-day authored complete album-palette arrangement, not simultaneous performance on every track. Existing fiddle, Hardanger and Norwegian langeleik construction presets are representative realizations; they do not identify the performers’ actual makes, string materials, sympathetic-string count or instrument regional manufacture. Microtonal guitar/mandolin, octave fiddle and munnharpe retain only their positive nominal identities with unspecified construction. No equal temperament or measured interval system is asserted; global tuning omitted. Bowed local-song melody is an authored technique choice. Studio and recording chain are authored, not reconstruction of Tou lyd.

extras.description: Malmin and Åshild Vetrhus album Med Åshild Vetrhus (7 March2025) explicitly documents traditional Rogaland repertoire, dance forms springar/halling/vals and religious songs learned from traditional sources and Ryfylke Museum archives. Full credits: Olav Christer Rossebø Hardanger fiddle, fiddle, microtonal mandolin; Anders Sundsteigen Hana microtonal guitar, munnharpe, langeleik, octave fiddle; Åshild Vetrhus voice. Eight positive roles retained, one credited vocalist. Octave fiddle retained from detailed credits despite omission in introductory list. Rogaland Musikk is a regional traditional repertoire subset, distinct from Rogaland Indie and broad Norwegian Folk/Nordic Folk; neither category is asserted equivalent. This documented full-album practice combines instrumental dances and sacred songs. Three players alternate eight role types across the album; the authored combined palette does not assert all eight sounded simultaneously. extras.description: BrookWright’s publisher description identifies Andrew Wainwright’s Illuminate as a seven-minute instrumental brass-band triptych commissioned for Chicago Staff Band’s 2015 England tour, with an International Staff Band performance link. Its full parts list contains E-flat/B-flat cornets, B-flat flugelhorn, E-flat horns, B-flat baritones, tenor and bass trombones, B-flat euphoniums, E-flat/B-flat basses, timpani and two additional percussion parts. No sung part is listed. The complete published concert work is modeled, not an arbitrary reduction of a larger band roster. All ten instrumental families remain, including distinct tenor horns and baritone horns. Additional percussion stays unspecified because the publisher does not enumerate implements; timpani is separately retained. Cornet and tuba cards represent families spanning the two scored keys, with authored B-flat archetypes and no claim that these remove the E-flat source parts or reproduce every sectional doubling. ArtMusic follows the positively described through-composed triptych and full published score, while its Salvation Army institutional category remains distinct from generic British brass band. This is not a claim every staff band programme is voiceless. Original legato brass defaults and unmuted trombone are authored settings; exact concert makers are unknown. Chicago is the commissioned band’s named institutional anchor, not the London premiere venue.

All17 positive families and24 vocalists retained; group voicing unspecified, no assumption24part counterpoint or singing throughout every track. The existing neutral alto/tenor/baritone saxophone section owner retains the full section: two alto, two tenor and one baritone players. Repeated brass players likewise do not require duplicate family IDs. Low-register tuba and sousaphone and both trombone types remain distinct. Party cans use a neutral isolated owner without material/mechanism invention. Additional generic percussion remains independently retained. Modern construction/defaults, unmuted trumpet/tenor trombone, coherent common legato wind/tenor-trombone/trumpet/sax-section articulation, accordion chordal vamp and wood-beater bass drum are authored arrangement settings, not measured original equipment. extras.description: Publisher explicitly identifies this mass as Tanzlmusi in the Inntaler/Hippacher setting. Complete available scoring comprises two flugelhorn lines, optional Bb clarinet, a tenorhorn/trombone/bass-trumpet alternative line, tuba and Harmonika. The selected realization retains both flugelhorn lines, includes the optional clarinet and chooses the expressly authorized trombone alternative. The publisher lists eight liturgical movements and identifies Fritzens church as the demonstration-recording locality. Complete named instrumental score realization including the optional clarinet, not the minimum quartet reduction and not a generic band inferred from the word Tanzlmusi. Alternate transposed parts duplicate musical lines; tenorhorn and bass trumpet are alternatives to the retained trombone, not omitted simultaneous roles. Two flugelhorn parts share one family card. No vocal staff or singer is specified in the publisher scoring; liturgical movement titles alone do not invent sung voices. Ritual-devotional placement applies only to this explicit mass branch, not all secular Tanzlmusi dance music. Bb flugelhorn/clarinet, CC tuba and unmuted tenor trombone implement stated scoring choices; accordion construction and classical wind phrasing are authored realizations rather than measured demonstration-session facts. extras.description: The government artist agency identifies the Berlin ensemble’s Tanzorchester tradition and explicitly enumerates its six-person Swing-Combo package: trumpet, saxophone, piano, double bass, drums and one vocal soloist. This full advertised formation is selected; larger orchestral and theatrical packages are separately documented. The ensemble’s dance-entertainment repertoire spans 1920s–1970s material and standard ballroom dances. One Bb trumpet, one tenor saxophone, concert grand, pizzicato double bass and brushed drum kit are authored timbral/construction choices; the agency leaves sax subtype, piano make and instrumental techniques unspecified. No electronic string substitute or extra keyboard is introduced. Punchy horn attacks, matched sax articulation and double-bass pizzicato are deliberate choices.
